newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - EBRD eyes Taiwan dollars.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - EBRD eyes Taiwan dollars.

text.p: Asian debt markets started the week slowly on Monday.

In news from Taiwan, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development plans to issue 5.5 billion Taiwan dollars (US$200 million) worth of Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds, lead underwriter Grand Cathay Securities said on Monday.
The lead said the issue was expected to have a tenor of seven-years but declined to release further details.
The EBRD would be the third development bank to issue Taiwan dollar bonds.
The Central American Bank of Economic Integration plans to issue T$6.8 billion (Us$246 million) Taiwan-dollar bonds on May 16.
The Asian Development Bank issued T$2.6 billion (US$100 million) worth of Taiwan dollar bonds in August 1995, and launched a T$7 billion (US$255 million) issue in December 1996.
In other news, a couple of Korean banks have mandated new issues.
Korea Long Term Credit Bank has mandated ABN Amro Hoare Govett and Sakura Finance Asia to arrange a US$100 million floating rate note issue, bankers said.
They said the facility has a final maturity of 364 days.
Price talk is around 43 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Bankers said that the deal offers good value at 43 basis points for one year.

With spreads for Korean bank issues widening, bankers said some borrowers have opted for short tenors with the idea that spreads will correct and they will be able to borrow more cheaply in coming months.

Bankers said Peace Bank Of Korea has mandated KDB Asia to arrange a US$40 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue. They said the facility has a final maturity of three years with put and call options in year two.
In the loan market, Hongkong Electric Co has increased the size of its two-tranche term loan facility to HK$5.0 billion from HK$3.5 billion following a strong response in syndication.
The facility had been oversubscribed to HK$6.0 billion, with 25 banks joining. HSBC Investment Bank was the sole coordinating arranger.
